rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child’s diplomatic cancellation message. Both open with emphatic regret, state that the anticipated visit had been awaited with pleasure, explain that overriding public responsibilities make the visit impossible, and express confidence that the affected parties will understand. The child adapts that sequence from the President canceling his own trip to acknowledging another president’s cancellation. C02 and C07 share visit-related diplomatic language, references to spouses or close bilateral ties, and anticipated discussions, but neither matches the cancellation-and-understanding structure as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It is with sincere regret that I have received Your Excellency's telegram in which you inform me that you have found it necessary to forego your plan to come to Washington
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I SEND YOU this message with exceeding regret... The turn of events yesterday leaves me no option... but to remain at the White House
shared_material.explanation: Both frame a canceled presidential visit through strong regret followed by unavoidable official circumstances.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Mrs. Eisenhower and I had been looking forward with keen anticipation to the personal pleasure of a visit
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I was looking forward with anticipation and pleasure to revisiting Texas
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive pairing of 'looking forward,' 'anticipation,' and 'pleasure' is closely shared.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I can well understand and appreciate the matters of overriding national importance which must perforce occupy the attention of the President
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I know that you... will fully understand the need for this change
shared_material.explanation: Both close the cancellation explanation by emphasizing understanding of the compelling reason for the change.
